messages.author: 7e9c32978ea78a1e
messages.subject: command line arguments?
parts:
Is it possible to pass scalar arguments to CmdStan from the command line? For example, something like

./dummymodel sample data file=input.data.R start_date=1960 end_date=1969

I'm trying to do a number of rolling estimations using subsets of a single panel dataset. It would be convenient to be able to use the same input data file and executable, and to have a script vary the output file and, say, the start and end dates for each estimation.

A command line argument would be one way to get this done. If that's not possible, any alternative suggestions?

Thanks!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] command line arguments?
parts:
No, but it wouldn't be hard to do something like this in bash:


cp input.data.R input_new.data.R
echo 'start_date <- 1960' >> input_new.data.R
echo 'end_date <- 1969' >> input_new.data.R
./dummymodel sample data file=input_new.data.R start_date=1960 end_date=1969

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] command line arguments?
parts:
> On Apr 16, 2015, at 8:00 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> No, but it wouldn't be hard to do something like this in bash:
>
>
> cp input.data.R input_new.data.R
> echo 'start_date <- 1960' >> input_new.data.R
> echo 'end_date <- 1969' >> input_new.data.R
> ./dummymodel sample data file=input_new.data.R start_date=1960 end_date=1969

You should remove the start_date and end_date from the final line.
It'll throw an error because CmdStan checks its arguments
carefully.

- Bob
